glosses: Se dice de un alimento que empalaga (causa fastidio o hastío), usualmente por ser demasiado dulce.

examples.text: Generalmente el exceso de azúcar resulta demasiado empalagoso.

glosses: Se dice de alguien que causa fastidio por ser excesiva o afectadamente dulce o amable.

examples.text: Tu amiga es una empalagosa, me aburre por ser excesivamente cariñosa

glosses: Sabor dulce que empalaga el gusto o el olfato, por ser muy azucarado.

examples.text: Este habano destaca por su sabor muy dulzón, que perdura en la boca durante toda la fumada acompañado de ligeros toques picantes. Su aroma sigue la misma línea. Es intenso a tabaco con tonos dulzones y recuerdos a hierba fresca y cuero

glosses: Alguien que es inocente, ingenuo o inmaduro. Asociado a la tierna o dulce infancia.
In a sick manner; in a way that reflects or causes sickness.

examples.text: sickly pale; to cough sickly

[…] he sickly guess’d
How lone he was once more, and sadly press’d
His empty arms together […]
The dazed man stared sickly at Casy.
For ten brutal minutes he was in torment, then the pain gradually eased. He felt sickly limp but relieved, thankful for his good health.
The creaseless horizontal face of the giant smiled sickly, leering.

Thus conscience does make cowards of us all,
And thus the native hue of resolution
Is sicklied o’er with the pale cast of thought,

Thy Drudge contrives, and in our full career
Sicklies our hopes with the pale hue of Fear;
[…]a cancer gnawing at the root of happiness, defeating every aim at permanent good in this world, and sicklying all sublunary joys[…]

He evidently thinks the sweet little innocents never heard or thought of such a thing before, and would go on burying their curly heads in books, and sicklying their rosy faces with “the pale cast of thought” till the end of time[…]
Ockham was critical of so many of his fellows for sicklying over theology with the obscurities of philosophy.

1889, Samuel Cox, An Expositor’s Notebook, London: Richard D. Dickinson, 7th edition, Chapter 26, p. 364,
But the seven most prominent Apostles […] still hang together, their hearts tormented with eager yet sad questionings, their hopes fast sicklying over with the pale hues of doubt.

examples.text: „In letzter Zeit sieht sie aber recht kränklich aus und fehlt hin und wieder im Laden.“

„Eines Tages fand er heraus, dass er nach dem Tod seines schon kränklichen Vaters ein Vermögen erben würde.“

„In seiner übergroßen Kleidung wirkte er noch schmächtiger und leidender, und seine Hände, die vom unteren Teil seiner Ärmelhalb verdeckt waren, sahen dünnund kraftlos aus, wie die eines Kindes, eines kränklichen kleinen Mädchens.“
